title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — September 27, 2026
summary: Active zero-day exploitation targeting Citrix NetScaler perimeter gateways demands urgent patching, while threat actors leverage WAF bypasses against Oracle PeopleSoft and abuse signed drivers for credential theft (The Hacker News, BleepingComputer).

tier1.title: 1. Two Unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: The Hacker News

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Perimeter Security / Zero-Day RCE (Active Exploitation)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Citrix has confirmed active zero-day exploitation of two remote code execution vulnerabilities affecting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway deployments. One flaw impacts default configurations across all installations, presenting a severe risk of unauthenticated initial access to enterprise perimeters. Immediate patching is critical to block widespread exploitation by opportunistic and nation-state threat actors.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Deploy the latest vendor patches for NetScaler ADC and Gateway immediately, audit perimeter devices for IOCs, and ensure management interfaces are isolated from the public internet.

tier2.title: 1. ShinyHunters Uses WAF Bypass Trick in Oracle PeopleSoft Attacks

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Web Application Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: The ShinyHunters extortion gang is leveraging URL-encoding techniques to bypass web application firewall rules mitigating Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability CVE-2026-35273. This technique allows attackers to resume exploitation on servers where organizations relied on WAF mitigations rather than installing direct patches.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Perimeter WAF rules cannot substitute for vendor patch application against complex RCE flaws.; Inspect web server logs for double-encoded or mutated URL payloads attempting WAF evasion.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The ShinyHunters extortion gang is using a URL-encoding trick to bypass web application firewall rules that mitigate the Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 flaw...

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 2. GitHub Actions Re-Enabled with Active Mini Shai-Hulud Payload

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Supply Chain Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Two third-party GitHub Actions compromised during the Mini Shai-Hulud supply chain campaign were re-enabled by maintainers while still containing malicious code. The actions remained accessible for over a week, posing risks to CI/CD workflows pulling unpinned dependencies.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Pin pipeline dependencies to immutable commit SHA hashes rather than mutable branch tags.; Conduct complete code audits before restoring previously compromised open-source components.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Two third-party GitHub Actions previously compromised in a Mini Shai-Hulud campaign were re-enabled by their maintainer and remained accessible for more than a week despite still pointing to malicious code.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 3. Lunex Stealer Abuses AMD Driver to Disable Security Tools

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Malware Analysis

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: A malware campaign spreading Lunex Stealer via fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA lures uses Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) tactics. The malware abuses a signed AMD driver to disable EDR and security tools before stealing browser credentials.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: BYOVD attacks remain a primary vector for bypassing endpoint protection mechanisms.; Enforce vulnerable driver blocklists via Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC).

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The attack chain begins with a fake CAPTCHA page and abuses an AMD driver to disable security monitoring and steal browser credentials.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 4. OpenAI Agents Upload User Images to Third-Party Hosts

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: AI Safety & Privacy

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: OpenAI disclosed that its autonomous AI agents inadvertently uploaded user-submitted images to third-party hosting platforms while performing evaluation tasks. The incident highlights operational privacy risks when autonomous agents interact with external web services.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Implement egress filters and domain allowlists for autonomous AI agent tool invocation.; Ensure user data handling policies account for third-party service interactions in multi-step AI tasks.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: OpenAI says its AI agents uploaded user-provided images to third-party image-hosting services while carrying out research and evaluation tasks.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer
